statement: The following facts concern only the critical nearest- neighbor model. 1. For bounded finitely connected domains without singleton boundary components and with finitely many nondegenerate fixed-plus, fixed-minus, or free boundary arcs, separated bulk spin and energy correlations converge with dimensions 1/8 and 1. Discrete domains converge in the Caratheodory sense, with eventually matching boundary-component and arc counts and converging boundary marks. Convergence is uniform on compact separated configurations. The limits are conformally covariant and continuous under these marked-domain limits. The energy convention initially subtracts its plane mean; expanding the finitely many subtractions gives the same assertion for domain-centered energies. The two bond directions have the same scalar limit. Homogeneous half-plane spin limits and full-plane spin limits are included, with odd plane correlations zero. 2. Normalize the continuum spin so that its plane two-point function is |z − w|−1/4. Write Gn for its n-point function. For even n, Gn,C(z1, . . . , zn)2 = 2−n/2 ∑ µ∈{−1,1}n ∑ i µi=0 ∏ i<j |zi − zj|µiµj/2 . (2.6) For zi in the upper half-plane, put qij = |(zi − zj)/(zi − zj)|. Then G+ n,H(z)2 = 2−n/2 ∏ i (2 Im zi)−1/4 ∑ µ∈{−1,1}n ∏ i<j q µiµj/2 ij , (2.7) Gfree n,H(z)2 = cn ∏ i (2 Im zi)−1/4 ∑ µ∈{−1,1}n ( ∏ i µi ) ∏ i<j q µiµj/2 ij , n even. (2.8) Here cn = (−1)n/22−n/2 for even n, including c0 = 1. The plus formula holds also for odd n; minus boundary is obtained by spin flip. These functions inherit reflection positivity from the lattice and satisfy spherical covariance in the plane. The plus-disk one-point functions of the spin and the plane-centered scalar energy are nonzero. 3. For homogeneous plus, minus, or free reference laws and for the plane, the rescaled two-point bound is δ−1/4 |Eσzσz′ | ≤ C(|z − z′ | ∨ δ)−1/4 on buffered compact sets. More generally, if z1, . . . , zn lie in a fixed compact interior set and ρi is the lesser of a fixed buffer radius and one quarter of the distance to the other insertions, then ⏐ ⏐ ⏐ ⏐ ⏐ E ∏ i σzi ⏐ ⏐ ⏐ ⏐ ⏐ ≤ Cn ∏ i ( δ ρi ∨ δ )1/8 . (2.9) 9 Repeated sites are allowed with the factor capped at one. The estimate uses ordinary FK wiring and homogeneous cluster coloring; prescribed mixed boundary signs are handled by buffered density comparison. For bounded compactly supported piecewise regular profiles h, the variables Xδ(h) = δ15/8 ∑ z h(z)σz have uniform exponential moments of every fixed real order under homogeneous reference laws on buffered compact sets. Positive-profile bounds follow from GHS; signed profiles follow by splitting the signs and applying Cauchy–Schwarz. These moment inputs also hold in homogeneous half-plane references by local comparison. 4. In a fixed square with free boundary and zero field, for every ϵ > 0 there are K < ∞ and c > 0 such that, for all sufficiently small δ, with probability at least 1 − ϵ a nearest-neighbor vertex circuit surrounds the concentric square of one third the side length. The circuit is contained in the union of at most K FK clusters, each of cardinality at least cδ−15/8; successive clusters may be separated by one nearest-neighbor step. For a uniform positive field hδ15/8, conditional on internal FK bonds, a cluster C is attached to the plus ghost with probability tanh(hδ15/8 |C|), (2.10) independently for distinct internal clusters. Internal bonds dominate their zero-field law. Consequently, at fixed physical square size, the probability of a plus-spin circuit tends to one by choosing a sufficiently large finite h and then a sufficiently small mesh.
